testable_competencies.absorption_factors: Identify factors that alter drug absorption and bioavailability (lipophilicity, surface area, molecular size, ionization/pH, drug transporters) and their clinical consequences.
testable_competencies.first_pass: Apply the concept of first-pass metabolism to explain why oral bioavailability differs from IV bioavailability (F=1) and why some routes (sublingual, rectal, transdermal) are chosen specifically to reduce first-pass exposure.
testable_competencies.p_gp: Recognize P-glycoprotein as a clinically relevant efflux transporter whose inhibition (macrolides) or induction (rifampin, St. John's wort) alters serum concentrations of its substrates (digoxin, apixaban, cyclosporine).

testable_competencies.barriers: Recognize the BBB and placenta as relative barriers relevant to CNS side-effect risk and fetal drug exposure.
testable_competencies.vd_interpretation: Interpret a drug's volume of distribution as reflecting its tissue vs. plasma distribution pattern (small Vd -> plasma/protein-bound; large Vd -> tissue/fat depot), and apply this to explain age-related Vd changes for lipophilic drugs.

entries.structural_rationale: 'Metabolism (Biotransformation)' heading confirmed on pdf page 179 (0179.json): sites of biotransformation, prodrug activation/toxic-metabolite examples, phase I (oxidation/reduction/hydrolysis, largely CYP-mediated) vs. phase II (conjugation) reactions, and genetic-polymorphism examples (CYP2D6 prodrug activators tamoxifen/tramadol/codeine, CYP2C9-metabolized warfarin). testable_competencies.biotransformation: Classify a drug-metabolism pathway as phase I (oxidation/reduction/hydrolysis, often CYP-mediated) or phase II (conjugation) and predict the consequence (activation of a prodrug, formation of a toxic metabolite, inactivation).
testable_competencies.cyp_interactions: Predict the clinical consequence of co-administering a CYP inhibitor or inducer with a CYP substrate drug (e.g., toxicity from inhibition, therapeutic failure from induction) using the named high-yield examples (macrolides, azole antifungals, grapefruit juice, rifampin, carbamazepine, St. John's wort).
testable_competencies.polymorphism: Recognize genetic CYP polymorphism (poor/ultra-rapid metabolizer) as a cause of unpredictable drug response, using the codeine/tramadol/tamoxifen (CYP2D6) and warfarin (CYP2C9) examples.

entries.title: Drug Metabolism and Cytochrome P450-Mediated Interactions

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective requires accounting for 'liver and renal function' when prescribing; this unit's renal-clearance-mechanism content (glomerular filtration, tubular secretion/reabsorption, transporter-competition interactions such as probenecid-penicillin) is the mechanistic basis for renal dose adjustment.

entries.structural_rationale: 'Excretion' heading confirmed on pdf page 180 (0180.json): renal clearance formula (glomerular filtration + tubular secretion - tubular reabsorption), age/disease effects on renal function, mechanisms of each renal process (including transporter-mediated secretion competition, e.g., probenecid inhibiting penicillin excretion), and non-renal routes (biliary/enterohepatic recirculation, pulmonary, minor routes including breast milk), ending immediately before the 'Pharmacokinetic Considerations' heading on the same page.

testable_competencies.renal_clearance: Apply the renal clearance formula (filtration + secretion - reabsorption) to explain why renal impairment reduces clearance of renally-eliminated drugs, and recognize transporter-mediated excretion interactions (e.g., probenecid delaying penicillin excretion).

testable_competencies.half_life: Apply the concept of elimination half-life to predict time to steady state (4-5 half-lives) and time to complete elimination after stopping a drug.
testable_competencies.kinetics_order: Distinguish first-order from zero-order (non-linear/saturation) elimination kinetics and recognize the clinical drugs where zero-order kinetics becomes relevant at therapeutic or toxic doses (phenytoin, alcohol, high-dose ASA).
testable_competencies.loading_dose: Recognize when a loading dose is indicated (long half-life and/or need for rapid therapeutic effect, e.g., amiodarone, digoxin, phenytoin) vs. when maintenance dosing alone suffices.

testable_competencies.therapeutic_index: Calculate/interpret the Therapeutic Index (TD50/ED50 or LD50/ED50) and apply the principle that a larger TI indicates a safer drug; recognize the named narrow-TI drugs that commonly require TDM (digoxin, theophylline, warfarin, lithium, cyclosporine).

entries.structural_rationale: GY.S05's printed title 'Fibroids' (extraction_method BODY_HEADING_CONFIRMATION, HIGH confidence) is body-confirmed but the node's inherited page range (609-612) and T-children (Hormonal Methods, IUD, Emergency Postcoital Contraception) belong to an adjacent 'Contraception' section that TOC extraction merged into the same node. Targeted raw-OCR verification of pdf pages 608-612 (undertaken as a follow-up coverage-gap investigation, not part of the original chapter pass) found: pdf page 608 (TN 'GY14') opens with an unambiguous fibroid-specific clinical section (Definition: 'benign smooth muscle tumour of the uterus'; Epidemiology; Pathogenesis), continuing through fibroid-specific management (GnRH agonists/antagonists, uterine artery embolization, myomectomy, hysterectomy) on pdf page 609 (TN 'GY15'); a body-confirmed 'Contraception' heading then begins mid-page-609, introducing the Hormonal Methods/IUD/EPC content already represented as SU-GY-10. Fibroids is therefore a genuine, separate body section with real clinical content of its own - not a cross-reference and not solely a Contraception mis-extraction - represented here as its own study unit against source node GY.S05, with a page range corrected to pdf 608-609 based on direct raw-OCR verification rather than the node's inherited (Contraception-derived) range. No MCC objective names 'fibroids' or 'leiomyoma' as its own presentation; MCC objective 2 ('Abdominal masses and pelvic masses') explicitly lists 'leiomyoma' among its Gynecologic causal conditions, so this unit is mapped as COMPONENT evidence rather than DIRECT.

entries.structural_rationale: Five T-children of 'Hemolytic Anemia' (Thalassemia, B-Thalassemia Minor, B-Thalassemia Major, B-Thalassemia Intermedia, a-Thalassemia; all LOW confidence, TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED) are consolidated into one unit: they are graded severities/genotypes of a single diagnosis category rather than independently tested competencies, consistent with the not-fragmenting-generic-subheadings instruction. Genotype-specific molecular/allelic detail (exact gene-deletion patterns) is kept at RECOGNIZE depth rather than CORE_ACTION.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize thalassemia trait/minor vs. major/intermedia by CBC pattern (low MCV with normal/high RBC count), ethnicity-based pretest probability, and Hb electrophoresis, distinguishing it from iron deficiency anemia.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize the transfusion/chelation-dependence spectrum and genetic counselling indication.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for sickle cell disease specifically (full-registry search for 'sickle cell' returned zero matches, a registry-coverage-gap pattern already documented in chapters E, G, GS, GM, GY); sickle cell disease's chronic hemolytic anemia component falls under objective 42-1's scope, and its 'risk factors for serious underlying conditions' rationale supports the vaso-occlusive/aplastic/sequestration crisis content, though SCD is not named in the retrieved excerpt.
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)

entries.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json node H.S22 carries the concatenated printed title 'Sickle Cell Disease Landmark Hematology Trials' with a recorded page range of H61-H62 (pdf 715-716). Raw OCR confirmation (clean-ocr/0675.txt-0677.txt) shows Sickle Cell Disease is a genuine, extensive major topic (definition, pathophysiology, HbSS/HbSC/HbAS clinical features, vaso-occlusive/aplastic/sequestration crisis management, hydroxyurea therapy, screening) immediately following H.S07.T05 (a-Thalassemia) within H.S07's own declared page range (H18-H24); clean-ocr/0715.txt-0716.txt instead confirms pdf 715-716 is genuinely 'Landmark Hematology Trials' (see SU-H-50). This unit is therefore cited against H.S22 (the node bearing this title) but with the page range corrected to its confirmed body location, per the same-node title-concatenation precedent set by GY.S12 and documented fully in this file's methodology_note.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize and initiate management of acute sickle cell crises (vaso-occlusive, aplastic, splenic sequestration, acute chest syndrome) as hematologic emergencies, including indications for exchange transfusion.
testable_competencies.prevention: Recognize preventive measures (vaccination, prophylactic penicillin in children, hydroxyurea) and screening for chronic complications (stroke risk, retinopathy, pulmonary hypertension).
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize sickle cell disease genotypes (HbSS, HbSC, HbS-beta-thal) and their chronic manifestations (hemolytic anemia, functional asplenia/infection risk, growth delay).

entries.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json node H.S22.T01 ('Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia', LOW confidence, TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED) carries a correct title but a recorded page range of H61-H62 inherited from its mis-scoped parent H.S22. testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish warm from cold AIHA using the direct Coombs (direct antiglobulin) test and blood film findings (spherocytes vs. agglutination), and identify primary vs. secondary causes (lymphoproliferative disease, SLE, drugs, infection).

entries.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json node H.S23 ('Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia', HIGH confidence, TOC_OCR) carries a correct title but a recorded page range of H63-H64 (pdf 717-718); its T01 'Microangiopathy (TMA)' is a redundant duplicate of the same content and of H.S10.T02 ('Thrombotic Microangiopathies (TMAs)', already covered by SU-H-26). Raw OCR (clean-ocr/0677.txt) confirms the genuine MAHA/TMA definition-and-etiology content (vasculitis, eclampsia/HELLP, malignant hypertension, drug- and infection-induced causes, cross-referencing TTP/HUS/DIC by page number) sits within H.S07's page range, immediately after AIHA. Consolidated into one unit citing both H.S23 and H.S23.T01 with the corrected page range; genuine TTP/HUS/DIC clinical management remain covered independently at SU-H-26 and SU-H-30. See methodology_note for the full page-range defect.
entries.study_unit_title: Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia / Thrombotic Microangiopathy (Definition and Etiology)

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize schistocytes on blood film as the hallmark of intravascular RBC fragmentation and generate a differential (TTP, HUS, DIC, malignant hypertension, eclampsia/HELLP, mechanical heart valve, disseminated malignancy, drug-induced) that routes to the specific-diagnosis units elsewhere in this chapter.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize hereditary spherocytosis (spherocytes, elevated MCHC, increased osmotic fragility) and hereditary elliptocytosis (elliptocytes) as intrinsic membrane-defect hemolytic anemias, and identify splenectomy as the definitive treatment for severe disease with pre-splenectomy vaccination.

testable_competencies.management: Identify and avoid triggering drugs/exposures; recognize that G6PD assay may be falsely normal during acute hemolysis (high reticulocyte G6PD levels).
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize X-linked G6PD deficiency presenting as episodic hemolysis triggered by oxidative stress (drugs, infection, fava beans), with Heinz bodies and bite cells on blood film.

entries.study_unit_title: Macrocytic Anemia: Vitamin B12 and Folate Deficiency

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Distinguish B12 from folate deficiency (elevated MMA and homocysteine in B12 deficiency vs. isolated elevated homocysteine in folate deficiency) and identify their major causes (pernicious anemia, malabsorption, dietary, medication-induced).
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize neurologic manifestations specific to B12 (not folate) deficiency and the risk of precipitating/worsening them with unrecognized folate-only replacement.

entries.title: Macrocytic Anemia: Vitamin B12 and Folate Deficiency

testable_competencies.physiology: Recognize the stages of hemostasis (vascular spasm, primary platelet plug, secondary coagulation cascade, fibrinolysis) as background for the bleeding- and clotting-disorder units that follow.

entries.structural_rationale: TOC heading 'Immune Thrombocytopenia' (LOW confidence, TOC_OCR_UNANCHORED), a T-child of 'Disorders of Primary Hemostasis'.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose ITP as a diagnosis of exclusion in a patient with isolated thrombocytopenia and mucocutaneous bleeding, distinguishing primary from secondary (drug-induced, lymphoproliferative, autoimmune-associated) ITP.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize indications for treatment (corticosteroids, IVIG, TPO-receptor agonists, splenectomy) based on bleeding severity and platelet count, and recognize when observation alone is appropriate.

testable_competencies.emergency_recognition: Recognize the pentad/features of TTP (microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, +/- neurologic changes, renal dysfunction, fever) and HUS (typically post-diarrheal, renal-predominant) as medical emergencies.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate urgent plasma exchange for suspected TTP without delaying for confirmatory testing, and recognize that platelet transfusion is generally contraindicated.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize desmopressin (DDAVP) and vWF-containing factor concentrates as management options.

entries.study_unit_title: Hemophilia A, Hemophilia B, and Factor XI Deficiency

entries.study_unit_title: Coagulopathy of Liver Disease and Vitamin K Deficiency

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize elevated PT/INR from decreased hepatic synthesis of factors II, VII, IX, X (liver disease) or from vitamin K deficiency/warfarin effect, and distinguish the two by response to vitamin K administration.

entries.structural_rationale: P.S02 ('Common Complaints') is an organizational header with no independent content of its own; its 14 children (T01-T14) are each a distinct, atomic presenting-complaint topic with its own definition/epidemiology/clinical-features/management structure and are represented as individual study units. testable_competencies.red_flags: Differentiate benign cyanotic/pallid breath-holding spells (provoked by anger/frustration or pain/surprise, brief LOC, spontaneous resolution) from seizure, and recognize the association with iron deficiency anemia (spells improve with iron supplementation) and the indication for cardiac evaluation (prolonged QT) when spells are atypical or there is a family history of syncope/sudden death.

testable_competencies.differential_and_red_flags: Work through the crying/fussy-infant differential systematically (feeding/behavioural, infectious, physical injury including hair tourniquet and non-accidental trauma, medication/vaccine reaction, neonatal withdrawal) and recognize that infantile colic is a diagnosis of exclusion in an otherwise well, thriving infant.

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: VSD is the most common CHD lesion and its classic finding (holosystolic murmur at LLSB, murmur intensity inversely related to defect size) is the paradigm teaching case for objective 62.

entries.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json's P.S05.T02 ('Acyanotic Congenital Heart Disease') is a single umbrella node, but raw OCR of pdf 1217-1219 (P21-P23) body-confirms it groups multiple genuinely distinct named lesions, each with its own definition/epidemiology/clinical-features/investigations/management subsection: Ventricular Septal Defect ('most common congenital heart defect, 30-50%'), Atrial Septal Defect (3 subtypes), Patent Ductus Arteriosus, Coarctation of the Aorta, Aortic Stenosis, and Pulmonary Stenosis. Per the instruction to split broad TOC nodes only when body evidence confirms distinct topics (and not to fragment generic sub-headings within one disease), each of these six named lesions -- which are independently testable diagnoses with their own diagnostic criteria -- is recovered as its own study unit under a synthetic UNCATALOGUED id, while P.S05.T02 itself is retained only as the parent umbrella reference in source_hierarchy_path.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize VSD by size-dependent clinical course (small VSD: asymptomatic, spontaneous closure; moderate-to-large VSD: CHF by 2 mo, holosystolic murmur at LLSB with mid-diastolic apical rumble, risk of late pulmonary hypertension if untreated) and the indication for surgical closure by 1 yr in large defects.

entries.title: Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: ASD's classic exam finding (wide, fixed split S2 with a pulmonic outflow murmur) is a paradigm teaching case for objective 62.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize the three ASD subtypes (ostium primum -- associated with Down syndrome; ostium secundum -- most common; sinus venosus), the fixed-split-S2 exam finding, and the high spontaneous-closure rate for small defects vs. elective closure for larger ones.

entries.title: Atrial Septal Defect (ASD)

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize PDA's association with prematurity, the continuous machinery murmur with bounding pulses/wide pulse pressure, and that indomethacin (prostaglandin-E2 antagonist) is effective only in premature infants, with catheter/surgical closure reserved for term infants or persistent/complicated PDA.

entries.title: Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: objective 9-1 (Hypertension) applies directly -- coarctation's classic finding is a blood-pressure discrepancy between upper and lower extremities (brachial-femoral delay), a key secondary-hypertension cause in children.
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/hypertension/

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize coarctation by blood-pressure discrepancy between upper and lower extremities (brachial-femoral delay, >20 mmHg difference raising suspicion), its association with bicuspid aortic valve and Turner syndrome, and that severe neonatal presentation is a ductal-dependent emergency requiring prostaglandin E1 to keep the ductus open.

entries.study_unit_title: Aortic Stenosis and Pulmonary Stenosis (Valvular Obstructive Lesions)

entries.title: Aortic Stenosis and Pulmonary Stenosis (Valvular Obstructive Lesions)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: Tetralogy of Fallot is the most common cyanotic CHD lesion and the classic teaching case for objective 19 (Cyanosis and hypoxia) in a neonate/infant, including the 'boot-shaped heart' CXR finding and hypercyanotic ('tet') spells.
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/

entries.structural_rationale: toc_inventory.json's P.S05.T03 ('Cyanotic Congenital Heart Disease') is a single umbrella node, but raw OCR of pdf 1219-1220 (P23-P24) body-confirms it groups multiple genuinely distinct named lesions, each with its own figure and definition/pathophysiology/management subsection: Tetralogy of Fallot, Transposition of the Great Arteries, Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return, Truncus Arteriosus, Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome, and Ebstein's Anomaly (the last as a labeled sidebar box with its own Etiology/Treatment). Each is recovered as its own study unit under a synthetic UNCATALOGUED id, matching the Acyanotic-CHD split rationale above; P.S05.T03 is retained only as the parent umbrella reference in source_hierarchy_path.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize Tetralogy of Fallot's four components (VSD, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, overriding aorta, RVH), boot-shaped heart on CXR, and hypercyanotic spell management (knee-to-chest positioning, oxygen, morphine, fluids).

entries.title: Tetralogy of Fallot

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: TGA is a ductal-dependent cyanotic lesion presenting with severe hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen at ductal closure -- a paradigm teaching case for objective 19, with the classic 'egg-shaped heart' CXR finding.
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/

entries.structural_rationale: See Tetralogy of Fallot unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Cyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; TGA is body-confirmed on pdf 1219-1220 (P23-P24) with its own definition, physiology (parallel systemic/pulmonary circulations, survival dependent on mixing via PDA/ASD/VSD), and management (prostaglandin E1, balloon atrial septostomy, arterial switch).

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize TGA's ductal-dependent physiology (progressive hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen as the ductus closes), egg-shaped-heart CXR sign, and the emergency management sequence (prostaglandin E1 to maintain ductal patency, balloon atrial septostomy, definitive arterial switch surgery).

entries.title: Transposition of the Great Arteries (TGA)

entries.structural_rationale: See Tetralogy of Fallot unit's structural_rationale for the full account of the Cyanotic CHD umbrella-node split; TAPVR is body-confirmed on pdf 1220 (P24) with its own definition, pathophysiology, and management (urgent surgical repair for severe cyanosis).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize TAPVR's pathophysiology (all pulmonary veins drain to the right-sided circulation; an ASD is obligatory for survival) and the classic 'snowman' heart silhouette on CXR.

entries.title: Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return (TAPVR)

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Component match: a less common cyanotic lesion relevant to objective 19's differential.
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service); https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/cyanosis-and-hypoxia/

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize truncus arteriosus's pathophysiology (single great vessel gives rise to the aorta, pulmonary, and coronary arteries, overlying a large VSD) and the need for surgical repair within the first 6 wk of life.

entries.title: Truncus Arteriosus

mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: HLHS is the most common cause of death from CHD in the first month of life and a paradigm ductal-dependent-systemic-circulation emergency for objective 19 -- circulatory shock/metabolic acidosis on ductal closure is a classic, high-stakes teaching point.

testable_competencies.diagnosis_and_management: Recognize HLHS as ductal-dependent for systemic circulation (shock and metabolic acidosis on ductal closure), and the emergency management sequence (intubation, metabolic-acidosis correction, IV prostaglandin E1 to maintain ductal patency, surgical palliation or transplant).

testable_competencies.safety_disposition: Determine appropriate disposition (voluntary/involuntary hospitalization vs. outpatient safety planning) based on risk stratification and identify when urgent intervention is required.

entries.structural_rationale: PS.S11 is a HIGH-confidence, TOC_OCR-anchored section (pdf1390-1391) with no T-level children in toc_inventory.json. Body-confirmed content spans a general overview/sleep-hygiene-and-management page (pdf1390, PS36) followed by Table 8 (pdf1391, PS37), a single summary table of major DSM-5 sleep-wake disorder categories (insomnia, hypersomnolence, narcolepsy, circadian rhythm, restless legs, substance-induced, breathing-related [OSA/central/hypoventilation], and parasomnias) with per-row management. Represented as one unit per the project's non-fragmentation guidance, since the source itself presents these as a single reference table rather than as separate full write-ups.
entries.study_unit_title: Sleep-Wake Disorders (Overview, Sleep Hygiene, and DSM-5 Categories)

testable_competencies.differential: Given insomnia or excessive daytime sleepiness, generate a differential across the DSM-5 sleep-wake disorder categories (dyssomnias, breathing-related, parasomnias) and recognize characteristic distinguishing features (e.g., cataplexy for narcolepsy, snoring/witnessed apneas for OSA).
testable_competencies.management: Recognize sleep hygiene and CBT for insomnia (CBTi) as first-line for chronic insomnia, and that non-benzodiazepine agents are generally preferred over benzodiazepines when pharmacotherapy is used.
